name: 3 John

overview.author: “The elder” (1), traditionally identified as John the apostle.
overview.audience: Gaius, a beloved believer known for his hospitality.
overview.setting: Traveling missionaries depended on churches for support. A domineering church leader, Diotrephes, refused to welcome them and opposed John’s authority.
overview.purpose: To commend Gaius for his faithfulness and hospitality, rebuke Diotrephes’s pride, and recommend Demetrius.
overview.structure: Commendation of Gaius (1–8), rebuke of Diotrephes (9–10), commendation of Demetrius (11–12), and closing (13–15).

items.title: Walking in truth and supporting missionaries

themes.title: Walking in Truth
themes.text: John’s greatest joy is to hear his children walk in the truth.

themes.title: Hospitality
themes.text: Supporting traveling believers makes us fellow workers for the truth.

themes.title: Imitation
themes.text: “Do not imitate evil but imitate good.”

themes.title: Good Testimony
themes.text: Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone.

christInBook.text: The missionaries went out “for the sake of the name,” that is, the name of Jesus Christ.
Supporting gospel workers makes believers fellow workers for the truth that is in Christ.
Doing good shows that a person is from God, the God revealed in Christ.

reflection: Who in your life brings you joy by walking in the truth?
How could you support missionaries or gospel workers this year?
Where might pride make you want to “put yourself first”?
Whose good example are you imitating?
What kind of testimony do you have among those who know you (12)?

chapterList.title: Fellow Workers for the Truth
chapterList.summary: The elder prays for Gaius’s health, as his soul is well. He rejoices that Gaius walks in the truth and has faithfully welcomed traveling brothers, even strangers, who went out for the sake of the Name; supporting them makes us fellow workers for the truth. But Diotrephes, who loves to be first, refuses to acknowledge John, spreads wicked talk, and puts out those who welcome the brothers. “Do not imitate evil but imitate good.” Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone. John hopes to see Gaius soon.
questions: What does John pray for Gaius (2)?
Why is supporting gospel workers so important (5–8)?
How did Diotrephes’s pride harm the church (9–10)?
What does it mean to imitate good (11)?

tagline: Support those who work for the truth; imitate good, not evil
readingPlan: 1 chapter: a short book you can read in one sitting, then work through the questions over a few days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
